clue.text: Rise up and fight daughter at the back

parts.note: to rear is to rise up on the hind legs
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: A rebellious instruction to stand up and do battle, with a daughter lurking in the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearward describes a position toward or at the rear, so it fits the phrase about being behind.

clue.text: Drink company

definitions.meaning: ... (also bevvy) is British slang for an alcoholic drink
a group or company, especially of girls or quails

explanation.surface: A firm that makes beverages.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevy is slang for a pint or similar tipple, and separately a collective noun for a gathering of people or birds.

clue.text: Said 'Don't move decoration'

indicators.note: the words are spoken aloud, so we want a word that sounds like the instruction

parts.note: Freeze! is the command meaning stay absolutely still

explanation.surface: Someone tells a decorator to stay still while admiring their work.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is an ornamental horizontal band along a wall, a kind of architectural ornament.

clue.text: One's rather old-fashioned cul-de-sac

parts.note: one is, said in the first person, is I'm
passé means out of date, somewhat behind the times

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being a bit dated, like a quiet dead-end street.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is literally a dead-end street, and figuratively a deadlock with no way forward.

clue.text: Large amount of clubs needing creative work pack

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
art is creative work
to load is to pack or fill up

explanation.surface: A golfer needs a lot of clubs and some artistic effort to fill a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartload is literally what a cart holds, and loosely a great quantity of anything.

clue.text: Brother's Wi-Fi rather dodgy

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A monk complains that his internet connection is unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A Whitefriar is a Carmelite friar, named for the white habit, and friars address each other as brother.

clue.text: Give instruction: sun acceptable when hot internally

indicators.note: the hot letter goes on the inside of the word for acceptable

parts.note: cool means fine or acceptable in casual speech
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A weather tip: sunshine is fine so long as the heat stays inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them, a verb synonym of instruct.

clue.text: Message from public transport: 'Introduction of electronic support needed'

indicators.note: the tram needs these letters inside it to be complete

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: A notice on a tram says it needs electronic support to start.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a written communication sent by telegraph, an old-fashioned kind of message.

clue.text: For this particular purpose, include white wine, it's said

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, so we want something that sounds like it

parts.note: to include is to add, and hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Instructions to add a dash of white wine for one specific dish.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK is the British name for Rhine white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase ad hoc means made or done for one specific need only.

clue.text: See 24 down
Joy, it's time to get into breathing out, having dropped an aitch!

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the shortened word
dropping a letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: exhalation is the act of breathing out
aitch is the name of the letter H

explanation.surface: Delight at managing to exhale with a Cockney accent, dropping the aitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dropped' removes H from EXHALATION, leaving EXALATION, and 'to get into' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaltation is a state of rapturous elation, close to joy; it is also the collective noun for larks.

clue.text: Joke leg manufactured for rambling group?

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A prank prosthetic leg is made for a walking club.
explanation.walkthrough: A rambling group is a walking club; the question mark flags that this gaggle is the noisy, disorderly kind, like geese.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaggle is a flock of geese, and loosely a disorderly crowd of people, which may ramble.

clue.text: Maybe seaweeds' improbable general age

indicators.note: an improbable arrangement is an unlikely one, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: It's unlikely that seaweeds have reached the age of a typical person.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweeds such as sea lettuce belong to the green algae, so they are an example.

clue.text: Winter feature spells end of Christmas present season

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: now is the present time
fall is the American word for the autumn season

explanation.surface: Something wintry marks the close of the Christmas gift-giving period.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow coming down is a typical sight of the cold months.

clue.text: Say, rather badly: 'Bread vs rocks'

definitions.note: say means for example: rather and badly are both instances, so the plural fits

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles over a rock-paper-scissors-style game of bread against rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example definition: 'rather' and 'badly' are words of the kind asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather and badly are both words that modify verbs or adjectives, the grammatical class named.

clue.text: Be prepared to shoot transport members

parts.note: to bear is to carry or transport
arms are limbs, or members of the body

explanation.surface: Someone carrying weapons in a vehicle full of members, ready to fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear arms is to carry weapons, ready for firing them.

clue.text: One who fancies commercial muck, right?

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
mire is mud or muck

explanation.surface: A cynic asks whether an advert is rubbish, and whether a fan would agree.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone attracted to another person, someone who takes a shine to them.

clue.text: Fantastic Mere Man is coming!

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly imaginative, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a gent is a man

explanation.surface: An excited announcement that a wonderful ordinary man is arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like praise of the man but is the anagram signal on 'Mere' alone (giving EMER); 'is coming' reads as an arrival but defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent means arising or coming into being, as in an emergent nation.

clue.text: Quickly passes 'Men's Trousers Feature' — heartless youth!

parts.note: the flies are the zipped opening at the front of trousers

indicators.note: a heartless word has lost its central letter

parts.note: a boy is a youth

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about trouser fashion, with a callous young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle O from BOY, leaving BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Time flies by when it passes rapidly; the phrasal verb means speed past.

clue.text: No miser needs special finish on everything

parts.note: an end is a finish
all means everything

explanation.surface: A generous soul wants a special final touch on all things.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendall is a spendthrift who spends everything, the opposite of a hoarding skinflint.

clue.text: Caper results in country's leader being replaced

indicators.note: the first letter of the country's name is swapped for another letter

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A stunt causes a nation's head of state to be ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader being replaced' says only that the F of FRANCE changes; the new letter P comes from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or dance about playfully, and to prance is to leap about in the same spirited way.

clue.text: Play the bongos again, possibly requiring backing to produce hit

indicators.note: backing means turning the word round to read the other way

parts.note: to drum again could be called to redrum, a made-up word

explanation.surface: A musician re-records the bongo part, needing a backing track for a hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: REDRUM is famous as MURDER backwards in The Shining. Hit here is the gangland verb for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit someone in gangster slang is to kill them, which is to commit murder.

clue.text: Art set in amalgam, a rectangular arrangement

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed in the middle of the mixture

parts.note: an amalgam is a mixture, a mix

indicators.note: to set letters is to arrange them, here in a new order

explanation.surface: An artwork fixed in an alloy, forming an oblong display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is easy to read as part of 'set in'; here it rearranges the art (to ATR), and 'in' alone signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers or elements in rows and columns.

clue.text: State Republican keen to suppress independent legislative body

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: to keen is to wail in mourning, to lament

explanation.surface: A politician from one state wants to silence an independent candidate in the assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is a law-making assembly; it is also the collective noun for owls.

clue.text: Has a dated appreciation of accommodation

definitions.meaning: to dig something is old slang for to like it
British informal for lodgings or rented rooms

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person enjoys their lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dig was 1960s slang for enjoy, and digs means rented rooms or lodgings.

clue.text: Pop music centre regenerated Mary's classic sitcom

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter
regenerated means formed anew, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A music centre restored by Mary is a classic of television comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic BBC sitcom about the Home Guard in the Second World War. A music centre is an old all-in-one stereo system.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad's Army ran on BBC television from 1968 to 1977 and is still regularly repeated as a much-loved comedy.

clue.text: Spell of cold weather eventually penetrating the joint

indicators.note: the letter goes into the middle of the joint

parts.note: a ham is a joint of meat

indicators.note: eventually points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cold snap finally gets into the joints.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is a magic spell or incantation; it is also the collective noun for goldfinches.

clue.text: Buckle in lid in defect construction

indicators.note: the bent letters are placed in the middle of the word for a defect

parts.note: a bug is a defect, as in software

indicators.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape, so these letters are distorted

explanation.surface: A faulty lid buckles during the building work.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: the first is anagram fodder for 'Buckle' (making ILDIN), and only the second is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A building is a construction such as a house; it is also the collective noun for rooks.
